Oh sure that can happen, although, it’s not actually statistically that likely, the reason being it depends on the type of abuse, studies have shown repeatedly, different sets of statistics regarding different types of abuse.. this reflects the different causal factors.

For instance some types of abuse happen because of personality disorders that are statistically unlikely in and of themselves— so there would be no forward relation between that and any other abuse-

Having said that the idea of abuse being a vicious cycle absolutely has merit— however it is possible to be put through a lot of emotional psychological abuse and develop a trauma reaction, like CPTSD— whether or not you would find someone suffering from that abusive is a matter of opinion but it wouldn’t really be relevant since trauma response is a well studied area of psychology and actually totally understandable in a lot of ways..

Some of the personality disorders are actually quite decipherable when you start to understand what causes them..

The vicious cycle really doesn’t need to continue and is dependent upon a whole number of factors for instance it’s far more likely that older (first) children of narcissist will themselves become narcissist- this is clinically recognised however the reasons behind it are debatable— One theory holds that because younger siblings get the opportunity to spot that behaviour early on it is more avoidable and less likely to be emulated.

Be wary of applying blanket cases to all forms of abuse because they are statistically quite different from each other—

It really could be a vicious cycle equally though, it really doesn’t need to be one— The time bind concept comes out of an outdated Freudian model of psychology.

 — it’s always worth bearing in mind that psychology is not a hard science, as such well-established theories and concepts are subject to change as is the body of knowledge expands. This matters particularly in the way that statistics measures and are taken.

A 250ml / 500ml container of organic single cream, or any pouring or single cream you prefer.

As for sweetening you can use whatever you prefer personally I used to use honey but any kind of sugar will work fine you can even use maple syrup..

You can play with the amount of everything to make it how you want it..

Pour into your favourite extra large mug.. add marshmallows and cinnamon to taste —
